methods.label: Reveal a perfect square
methods.explanation:
The denominator requires \(x\ne0\). For every such real \(x\), the radicand is positive. Combining its terms over a common denominator reveals a perfect square:
\[
\begin{aligned}
1+\left(\frac{x^4-1}{2x^2}\right)^2
&=\frac{4x^4+(x^4-1)^2}{4x^4}\\
&=\frac{x^8+2x^4+1}{4x^4}\\
&=\left(\frac{x^4+1}{2x^2}\right)^2.
\end{aligned}
\]
The principal square root of a square is its absolute value. Since \(x^4+1>0\) and \(2x^2>0\), the quotient is positive, so
\[
\sqrt{1+\left(\frac{x^4-1}{2x^2}\right)^2}
=\frac{x^4+1}{2x^2}
=\boxed{\frac{x^2}{2}+\frac{1}{2x^2}}.
\]
This is choice \(\boxed{\text{E}}\), valid throughout the original domain \(x\ne0\).
